title: Course final
sub: Server, window and game: one mechanism
cards/0/task: Find the platform where .Result doesn't hang.
cards/1/task: A Unity script moves a transform after await. Make it all work without freezing frames.
cards/2/q: What do WPF and Unity have in common when it comes to async?
cards/2/options/0: Both install a SynchronizationContext that returns the continuation to the main thread
cards/2/explain: That's also why .Result hangs in both.
cards/3/q: Where is ConfigureAwait(false) dangerous? Select all that apply.
cards/3/options/0: In a WPF handler that then changes a control
cards/3/options/1: In a Unity script that then touches a transform
cards/3/explain: In a library it helps, and in ASP.NET Core it changes nothing.
cards/4/explain: Without destroyCancellationToken the wait won't be canceled, and the next line will touch a destroyed object.
cards/5/q: An ASP.NET Core server responds slower and slower under load, and the CPU is nearly idle. What do you suspect first?
cards/5/options/0: Blocking .Result/.Wait() calls ate up the pool threads
cards/5/explain: Pool starvation. Use await all along the chain.
cards/6/q: Put the path of a continuation after await in WPF in order
cards/6/items/1: The operation completed on a pool thread
cards/6/items/2: The continuation was posted to the context (Post)
cards/6/items/3: The UI thread took it from the message queue
cards/6/items/4: The code after await ran on the UI thread
cards/6/explain: If the UI thread is blocked on .Result at that moment, step 4 never happens. That's the deadlock.
cards/7/q: Match each platform to its context
cards/8/q: The main rule of the whole course?
cards/8/options/0: Async all the way: don't block async code with .Result and .Wait()
